subject: SKU split, broker fee handling, and list-price routing for Azure private offer
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmehealth.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.inference>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on Azure private offer packaging + broker fee treatment

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is starting to compile the docs for the Azure private offer and we have two items we need clarity on before we proceed to internal approvers:

1) SKU / line-item strategy: Acme needs to understand whether the private offer can list two distinct line items ("Platform" subscription + "Managed Onboarding") so we can show a clean platform list price while allowing a pass-through for services. If we keep everything on a single SKU, our internal finance team will flag it as a single charge and may push back.

2) Broker / reseller fee handling: our broker (CloudBroker) expects to invoice a separate brokerage fee. We need to confirm if Redwood will allow that fee to be externalized (i.e., invoice from CloudBroker directly to Acme) without affecting the private offer list price and any partner margin calculations. In short: can the broker fee be passed outside the PO revenue bucket?

I've attached our procurement questionnaire and the standard PO template (Acme-Procurement-Questionnaire.pdf).

Quick ask: can you confirm both points in writing? If helpful, we can do a 30-min call with vendor ops to lock down the mapping.

Best,

Maya Singh
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Health

Attachments: Acme-Procurement-Questionnaire.pdf

From: connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.inference>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmehealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on Azure private offer packaging + broker fee treatment

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear note and the questionnaire. Looping in Ben (Partnerships) and Laura (Sales Ops) to make sure we cover channel & invoicing.

Short answers up front:
- SKU / line-item: Yes — we can publish the private offer with separate line items ("Redwood Platform — runtime" + "Redwood Services — onboarding & support") so that list price on the platform reflects platform-only pricing while managed services appear as a distinct charge. That approach tends to smooth Acme's internal approval since platform spend and services are accounted separately.

- Broker fee: We can support an externally invoiced broker fee, but there are two sensible patterns depending on your preference:
  * Pass-through line item (recommended): create a separate "broker_fee" line item outside the private-offer revenue stream; CloudBroker invoices Acme directly for that fee. The private offer list price and discounting remain unchanged, and partner uplift calculations don't include the pass-through fee.
  * Included in list price (less ideal): include broker margin inside the services line item so that Redwood invoices the full amount and remits a commission to the broker. This affects channel uplift math and requires fee/commission mapping in our billing flow.

I attached a quick sketch of SKU mapping we typically use (proposed_sku_mapping.csv).

Next steps I propose:
1) 30-min call (vendor ops + procurement + broker) to confirm which pattern Acme prefers.
2) If pass-through, Ben will confirm partner commission treatment and provide language for the PO.
3) If included, Laura and finance will draft invoice & remittance flow and we will surface any tax implications.

Are you available tomorrow morning for a call?

—Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: proposed_sku_mapping.csv

From: Victor Chen <victor.chen@cloudbroker.io>
To: connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.inference>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on Azure private offer packaging + broker fee treatment

Connor / Maya — Victor from CloudBroker here. Appreciate the transparency Connor. A couple of clarifying questions from our side before the vendor call:

1) Channel uplift calc: When Redwood reports partner uplift / margin, is that calculated on gross list price before discounts, or on net revenue after you apply private-offer discounts and platform-level promotions? Our commission model ties to the net platform revenue so we need to ensure alignment.

2) Eligibility for commission: If the broker fee is pass-through (external invoice), will CloudBroker still be eligible for any success-based commission on platform ARR, or does pass-through explicitly remove that revenue from the partner compensation pool?

For context, I've attached an anonymized sample invoice showing a separate brokerage line (example-broker-invoice.pdf). If we can agree that pass-through broker fees won't reduce the base used for partner commission, that will make internal approvals much faster.

Happy to join a call tomorrow. Proposed window: 09:30–10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Victor Chen
Partnerships — CloudBroker
victor.chen@cloudbroker.io

Attachment: example-broker-invoice.pdf

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
To: Victor Chen <victor.chen@cloudbroker.io>, connor_obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.inference>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on Azure private offer packaging + broker fee treatment

Victor / team — quick note from Partnerships / Revenue ops to be explicit about how Redwood treats this:

- Partner uplift basis: Redwood calculates partner uplift and commission on net platform revenue after customer-facing discounts tied to the private offer (so net revenue = list price - PO discount). Platform promotions that are not part of the private offer will be excluded.

- Broker fee treatment: If CloudBroker is invoicing a separate, external "broker_fee" line item directly to Acme, we will treat that amount as a non-revenue pass-through for Redwood. It will not be included in the net revenue base used for partner uplift/commission calculations.

Operational implications:
- For pass-through: Finance/legal will need the broker's W-9 (or equivalent) and a brief SOW specifying the broker fee terms so we can document the non-revenue status.
- For included: If you want Redwood to invoice the broker fee and remit commission, we will need to model the commission (rate and timing) and run a quick tax/treaty check for cross-border flows.

Connor: please schedule the 30-min call and include Revenue Ops (I will join). Laura, please prep the sample contract language that says "broker fee is outside of Redwood revenue unless explicitly included in the PO."

Thanks — happy to push to a short SLA-friendly doc that Procurement can attach to the private offer.

Ben Carter
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.inference
+1 650-555-0199
